Sample N rows from a Cartesian product with optional correlation

Source: R/levels.R
link_levels.Rd

Draws N rows from the cross-product of the specified levels. When rho or sigma is non-zero, row assignments are correlated via a Gaussian copula so that units with high values on one level's variable tend to be paired with units with high values on the other level's variable.

Usage

link_levels(N, .by, ..., rho = 0, sigma = NULL)

Arguments

N

Number of rows to sample from the product.

.by

Character vector of level names, usually two.

...

Additional column expressions evaluated after linking.

rho

Scalar correlation of the Gaussian copula that links the levels' row assignments (default 0 = independent). It is not the realized rank correlation, which is smaller by the copula's own relation, \((6/\pi)\arcsin(\rho/2)\): rho = 0.7 lands at 0.68 and rho = 0.3 at 0.283. Ignored if sigma is provided. Comes after ..., so a column called r or s is a column and not a partial match.

sigma

Square correlation matrix (dimension = length(.by)).

Value

A fabricatr_level object, meaningful only as a named argument to fabricate. It contributes N rows drawn from the same product cross_levels would build, with replacement, so a combination can appear more than once and others not at all, and N may exceed the size of the product. Columns are as for cross_levels.

Details

The correlated draw takes one code path, so a given seed produces the same data on every machine. fabricatr 1.x switches to mvnfast::rmvn() when that package is installed, and passes it a core count, so its numbers move when either changes. This is the second and last place where 2.0 can give different numbers than 1.x, and it only differs when mvnfast is installed.

Examples

fabricate(
  primary   = declare_level(N = 20, p_quality = runif(N, 1, 10)),
  secondary = declare_level(N = 15, s_quality = runif(N, 1, 10)),
  students  = link_levels(
    N = 200, .by = c("primary", "secondary"), rho = 0.5,
    score = p_quality + s_quality + rnorm(N)
  )
)
#> # A tibble: 200 × 6
#>    primary p_quality secondary s_quality students score
#>    <chr>       <dbl> <chr>         <dbl> <chr>    <dbl>

#>  4 09           4.21 05             3.70 004       7.58
#>  5 03           4.12 02             6.25 005       9.44
#>  6 14           3.36 01             4.87 006       7.87
#>  7 19           2.14 09             8.83 007      12.7 
#>  8 05           4.94 08             9.97 008      15.6
